* **Swarm journey cards** — prices the journey's next run across its live targets.

The tool
tip shows a headline figure and a per-model or per-component breakdown. Copy varies by how well-grounded the estimate is:\n\n| Cop
y | Meaning |\n| - | - |\n| Estimated: \\~N credits — based on your recent runs | Full coverage, grounded in your own run history
|\n| Estimated: \\~N credits — partly based on recent runs | Full coverage, partially grounded in history |\n| Rough estimate: \\~
N credits — improves after first run | Full coverage, heuristic only (no history yet) |\n| At least \\~N credits — part of this ru
n is unpriced | Some models or run slices could not be priced |\n| Estimate unavailable for these models | No pricing data availab
le |\n\n1 credit = \\$0.01. Your free daily allowance and any BYOK keys change what is actually deducted. The estimate is informat

ional only — it never blocks or gates a run.

### Frozen execution snapshots

### Cost

Every iteration carries the MCPJam-b
illed cost of the model work it did,\npriced when the trial finished and stamped with the rates used — so a run's\ncost does not m

ove later when prices change. It rolls up onto cases, runs and
the metric strip.

A dash (`—`) means **no cost was observed**,

never that the trial was free:

| Why | What you see |
| - | - |
| Your own API key (BYOK) | MCPJam did not bill it, so there
is no cost to report. |\n| A harness run (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) | A harness turn mixes models — sub-agents on cheaper models
under a main one — and the trial's totals carry no per-model split, so no honest single figure exists. Harness cost arrives with

billed attribution. |
| No token usage reported | Nothing to price. |

A cost your own SDK runner reported is shown but labelle

d **runner** — it is
real, but MCPJam neither computed nor verified it.

When only some of a run's trials were priced, the tota
l says so. That\ndistinction matters most in CI: a run that looks cheaper may simply be a run\nwe priced less of, which is why the
compare API reports coverage counts\nalongside the cost and a cost gate treats partial coverage as non-gateable\nrather than as a

pass.

### Run view

While a run is in progress, the run header shows a **HOLD** or **SHIP** pill for each client/model pairi
ng to indicate the current trajectory. All pairings that share the same decision are grouped into one pill — a single **HOLD** pil
l lists every client not yet on track to pass, and a **SHIP** pill lists every client on track to pass. Intermediate states (**Run
ning**, **Grading**, **Inconclusive**) each get their own pill. Once a run finishes, these pills are removed from the header. The
**Compare runs** and **Run again** buttons are visible directly in the header.\n\n**Cancelling a run:** while a run is in progress
(status `pending`, `running`, or `grading`), a **Cancel run** button replaces **Run again** in the run header. Clicking it stops
every client-model pairing of that launch at once — runs that have already finished are skipped. A run still in `grading` (trials
done, gating judge still running) can also be cancelled. Once cancelled, stopped trials are recorded as `cancelled` rather than as
failures, so the run result reflects a deliberate stop rather than a test failure. The **Cancel run** button is also available in
the suite header when any run in the suite is still going. On the **Evals** tab, where the run detail is folded into the suite bo
dy rather than shown with a full header, the **Cancel run** button appears in the run-level action row (alongside Share, Export, a

nd Submission report) instead.
